seoTitle: How to Connect Jira to Google Sheets for Live Reports
metaDescription: Use the Jira Cloud for Sheets add-on to pull real-time issue data into Google Sheets and build automated sprint reports with JQL queries.
intro: Manually exporting Jira data every time you need a fresh sprint report is inefficient when a direct integration exists. The Jira Cloud for Sheets add-on connects your Atlassian workspace to Google Sheets, letting you pull live issue data and run custom queries. This guide covers installation through setting up automated refreshes.

steps.heading: Install the Jira Cloud for Sheets add-on
steps.body: Add the official extension from the Google Workspace Marketplace to your spreadsheet.

steps.heading: Connect your Atlassian account
steps.body: Authenticate and link your Atlassian workspace site to the add-on.

steps.heading: Run an initial data import
steps.body: Import project fields and issues from scratch to populate your spreadsheet.

steps.heading: Use starred filters for faster pulls
steps.body: Reference your saved Jira filters to speed up future data imports.

steps.heading: Write a custom JQL query
steps.body: Use the sidebar to filter issues by status, assignee, or other criteria with a custom JQL query.

steps.heading: Set up automated refreshes
steps.body: Activate a daily or hourly refresh schedule so your report stays current with live Jira data.

faq.question: Do I need to know JQL to use this integration?
faq.answer: Basic familiarity with JQL helps for advanced filtering, but you can also rely on starred filters from Jira to pull data without writing custom queries.

faq.question: Will my report update automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, you can configure automated hourly or daily refresh schedules so your Google Sheets report reflects the latest Jira data.

faq.question: Is this add-on official or third-party?
faq.answer: The tutorial refers to the official Jira Cloud for Sheets extension available through the Google Workspace Marketplace.

faq.question: Can I filter by assignee or issue status?
faq.answer: Yes, custom JQL queries let you filter imported issues by status, assignee, or other Jira fields.
